facts.label: Ritter's formula: binding energy of a polytrope
facts.display: U = 3/(5 − n) × GM²/R; n = 0 (uniform) gives 0.6, n = 1 gives 0.75

sources.title: Lynden-Bell & O'Dwyer (2001) One mass-radius relation for planets, white dwarfs and neutron stars, arXiv:astro-ph/0104450 (PDF; preprint, states Ritter's formula)

facts.notes: Lynden-Bell & O'Dwyer, section 3: "The gravitational potential energy is −αGM^2/R where Ritter's formula tells us that for polytropes α = 3/(5−n)", with "n = 0 corresponding to the homogeneous case". A classical textbook result (Ritter 1880; Chandrasekhar 1939); the source fetched is an arXiv preprint with no journal reference. Lane-Emden integration (researcher, skeptic and compiler): n = 0.98 gives α 0.746 and I/MR^2 0.2638; n = 1 gives 0.7500 and 0.2614; n = 1.1 gives 0.769 and 0.2494. Skeptic confirmed.

facts.page_short: the energy to blow Pluto apart
facts.notes: Energy to scatter all of Pluto to infinity. Uniform ball 3GM^2/(5R), G = 6.6743e-11 (existing gravitational_constant), M = 1.303e22 kg, R = 1,188.3 km: 5.72e27 J, a strict lower bound. Pluto is 65.5% rock by mass with an ice mantle of "~300 km" (Stern et al.). A two-layer model with an 888-900 km core (2,800-3,100 kg/m^3; hydrated rock) under ice or water at 950-1,100 kg/m^3 gives 6.32-6.50e27 J; packing all the anhydrous rock into a denser 820-850 km core gives up to 6.71e27. Value 6.5e27 J. Ice density assumed, not sourced; ignores porosity and compression. Spread under 20%: firm enough for a plain multiple. Skeptic: value lowered from 6.6e27 to match the source's 300 km mantle.

facts.page_short: the impact that made the Moon
facts.notes: Centre-of-mass collision energy 0.5 μ v^2, μ = mM/(m+M), from Carter et al. Table 1 (Earth masses of 5.9722e24 kg): canonical 0.90 + 0.13 at 9.2 km/s = 2.9e31 J; similar-mass 0.57 + 0.47 at 9.7 = 7.2e31; spinning proto-Earth 1.05 + 0.05 at 20 = 5.7e31; partial accretion 0.75 + 0.30 at 11.3 = 8.2e31. These reproduce the paper's Q_S within 1%. Abstract: "the specific impact parameters are under debate". Value 4.8e31 is the geometric middle, not a best estimate. Leaves out the gravitational energy released as the bodies merge (Table 1 Epot,0−Epot,min = 1.2-5.0e31 J). Skeptic: display now says four example impacts from one study, not every proposal. Alternative only (rough, sits on the Sun-day).

facts.page_short: the energy to blow Earth apart
facts.notes: Update of the existing key in final-environment.json (status claimed to derived). U = ∫G m(r) dm / r over PREM's 13 layers: integrated from the GENIE coefficients by the researcher (2.488e32 J) and the skeptic (2.4889e32 J; 2.488e32 scaled to NASA's 5.9722e24 kg), as in the existing energy_earth_binding_prem_computed (2.4904e32). PREM's own mass comes out 5.9732e24 kg and I/MR^2 0.3308, matching NASA. Uniform 3GM^2/(5R) = 2.24e32 J is a strict lower bound. Caveat: the coefficients are a code transcription of Dziewonski & Anderson 1981; the paper was not fetched. Skeptic: upgrade confirmed; the CitcomS cross-check had no URL and is dropped. Wikipedia kept as a cross-check only.

gaps: None within the band from the Sun-second (3.8e26 J) to Jupiter's binding energy (2.6e36 J) if the page shows either a multiple of the rung below or a share of the rung above: every step is at most 17x. Steps over about 10x (they break the rule only if the page shows multiples of the rung below alone): the Sun-second to Pluto (17x; an energy of 4-6.5e27 J would need 10-17x), and Earth's binding energy to Earth's orbit (10.6x, marginal). A cheap fix for the first: the Sun's output for ten seconds (3.8e27 J, luminosity x 10 s), not compiled. Below the band: Chicxulub (4.2e23) to the Sun-second (3.8e26) is about 900x; another band must fill it. Above the band: nothing past 2.6e36 J here. The next rung must be within about 10x (2.6e37 J) and no further than 100x (2.6e38 J); the Sun's output for a thousand years (1.2e37 J) would serve if the stellar band leaves a hole.
